detail: supported
Uses pretrained volume rendering priors (UDF) to push Gaussians toward true surfaces by optimizing along increasing rendering weights, avoiding off-surface drift and discreteness [S2].

The claim accurately reflects the content of Source [S2]. The source explicitly states that the method uses 'pretrained volume rendering priors' (specifically a UDF field) to 'push the Gaussians toward the true surfaces' by optimizing them. It mentions that this approach avoids the issues of 'discrete and sparse Gaussian representations' (discreteness) and guides Gaussians toward true surfaces rather than relying on self-distilled constraints that might lead to drift or degeneration. The source also notes that this is done by optimizing along the direction implied by the UDF/weighting, effectively addressing off-surface drift and discreteness issues inherent in standard Gaussian Splatting.
supported
Encourages consistency between SDF and 3DGS to enhance geometry reconstruction quality [S1].

The claim states that the method encourages consistency between SDF and 3DGS to enhance geometry reconstruction quality. The evidence explicitly mentions that '3DGSR [175] and GSDF [176] also encourage the consistency between SDF and 3DGS to enhance the geometry reconstruction quality.' Additionally, the passage describes a method that 'encourages Gaussians’ signed distance values to be zeros and the normal directions of 3DGS and the NeuS method to be as consistent as possible,' which aligns with the concept of encouraging consistency between SDF and 3DGS for better geometry. Therefore, the evidence fully supports the claim.
